name: sol_basics_vi_svi_13
description: Signed immutable integer variables shorter than 256 bits corrupted by buggy Solidity compiler (0.6.5-0.8.8)
question: The source file in `source` declares a pragma solidity version between 0.6.5 and 0.8.8 (inclusive) and defines at least one immutable state variable of a signed integer type narrower than int256 (e.g. int8, int16, int32, int64, int128), where this variable's value could be corrupted with invalid higher-order bits due to the compiler's signed-immutable packing bug, excluding cases where the pragma is outside this vulnerable range, the immutable variable is int256/uint256 or unsigned, or the file already restricts itself to a fixed non-vulnerable compiler version.
criteria: pragma solidity ^0.8.4; contract C { int128 public immutable value; constructor(int128 v) { value = v; } }
pragma solidity 0.6.8; contract Vault { int64 immutable cap; constructor(int64 _cap) { cap = _cap; } }
pragma solidity >=0.6.5 <0.8.9; contract Config { int32 immutable threshold; constructor(int32 t) { threshold = t; } }
pragma solidity 0.8.7; contract Token { int16 immutable rate; constructor(int16 r) { rate = r; } function getRate() external view returns (int16) { return rate; } }
